description.narrative:
Project seeks to advance inclusive youth-responsive natural resources governance in Binga Rural District, Zimbabwe. Despite their significant population, youths are systematically excluded from natural resources decision-making, law and policy formulation, and benefit-sharing mechanisms. The project addresses both structural and normative barriers to youth representation and meaningful inclusion in Binga's natural resources governance. It strengthens youth participation capacity, youth procedural rights awareness, establishes inclusive governance platforms, and advocates for youth representation quotas within local natural resources governance systems. Through intergenerational dialogues, legal and policy gap analysis, and targeted advocacy, project willpromote reforms in both formal governance frameworks and traditional structures. Binga will serve as a pilot case to inform broader national policy reform for youth meaningful representation in natural resources governance in Zimbabwe.
Project institutionalises meaningful youth participation and representation in biodiversity governance in Binga. It establishes inclusive governance platforms, builds youth capacity on governance procedural rights, laws, and advocacy, and promotes youth-responsive policyreforms. Key activities include youth advocacy training, development of an advocacy toolkit, multi-stakeholder policy dialogues, establishing a Youth Biodiversity Governance Forum, youth inclusion legal and policy gap analysis, policy brief and model policy for mandatory youth inclusion, community consultations, and a high-level policy advocacy launch to advance youth inclusion in biodiversity governance.

participating-org.narrative:
Earth Co-Existence Initiative is a youth-led organisation advancing environmental conservation, climate action, and socio-economic empowerment through green jobs, alternative livelihoods, and rights-based law and policy advocacy. Our work spans biodiversity, climate and renewable energy, and natural resources governance, integrating conservation science, social sciences, and legal-policy advocacy to strengthen community rights and promote harmony between people and nature. Our mission is to bridge law, policy, science, and practice in driving environmental conservation and climate action. Our vision is a Zimbabwe where empowered communities, youth leadership, and science-based laws enable sustainable natural resource use, equitable benefits, and thrivingecosystems. Our objectives are to implement practical conservation and climate solutions, drive evidence-based legal and policy reforms, build the capacity of youth and communities, and support government and stakeholder efforts. Our values are Stewardship, Collaboration, Innovation, Equityand Inclusion, and Integrity.
Our organization is youth-led by design, with young people holding full authority in both governanceand operations. At the governance level, 90% of our Board members are aged 18–35, and they exercise substantive decision-making powers, including strategic oversight, policy formulation, financial governance, and supervision of the Executive Director. This ensures that youth directly shape the organization's long-term direction and accountability systems. Operationally, the organization is entirely youth-managed. The Executive Director and all staff fall within the 18–35 age range, meaning young people lead program design, implementation, advocacy, resource mobilization, and partnerships. Youth, therefore, influence 100% of organizational decisions, from daily management to strategic planning. This ensures that our mandate, priorities, and impact are grounded in youth perspectives, lived realities, and leadership, making the organization authentically and structurally youth-led.
